q: At the quarterly review of a shop, the on-cost actually collected on the shop's On-Cost Work Order is found to be more than the on-cost absorbed into jobs at the pre-determined rate. The correct conclusion and action are:

options.A: There is over-absorption, and the shop's on-cost rate is reduced at once
options.B: There is under-absorption, and the quarterly review raises the shop's on-cost percentage for the next period
options.C: There is under-absorption, and the difference is debited to the jobs completed in the quarter
options.D: The difference is ignored, because pre-determined rates are never revised

e: Actual overhead exceeding the amount recovered at the pre-determined rate is under-absorption; the quarterly review corrects it by raising the rate for the next period.

q: A workshop executes a deposit work for an outside body and bills it at works cost plus pro-forma on-cost only. An Accounts objection points out that the bill under-recovers the Railway's dues. The elements still missing from the price are:

options.C: Neither — works cost plus pro-forma on-cost is the full price for outsiders
options.D: Supervision charges at 12.5% and the profit element

e: Work for outsiders is priced above works cost: pro-forma on-cost, supervision charges (12.5%) and profit are all added, otherwise the Railway under-recovers.

q: The pro-forma on-cost charges collected on deposit works executed for outside parties are credited to:

options.B: The WMS account of the workshop

e: Pro-forma on-cost, the notional overhead levied on work for other departments and outsiders, is credited to Earnings (Abstract Z) when collected.

q: A job is costed with direct labour Rs 40,000 and direct material Rs 55,000. Shop on-cost is 60% and general on-cost is 15%, both on direct labour. The total (works) cost of the job is:
e: Shop on-cost is Rs 24,000 and general on-cost is Rs 6,000; works cost = prime cost Rs 95,000 + Rs 30,000.

q: A POH job card summary shows direct labour of Rs 72,000 and direct material of Rs 1,08,000 booked to the job. The prime cost of the job is:
e: Prime cost is direct labour plus direct material only; on-cost is added afterwards to arrive at works cost.

q: The direct labour booked to the jobs of a shop is Rs 85,000. At the pre-determined shop on-cost rate of 60% on direct labour, the shop on-cost absorbed into those jobs is:
e: Shop on-cost is absorbed at 60% of the direct labour charges of the shop's jobs.

q: A shop manufactures a batch of 200 identical components. Direct labour is Rs 80,000, direct material Rs 1,20,000, shop on-cost 60% of direct labour and general on-cost 15% of direct labour. The unit cost per component is:
e: Total job cost is Rs 2,60,000; divided over the batch of 200 components, the unit cost is Rs 1,300.

q: During a quarter, direct labour booked to a shop's jobs is Rs 12,00,000 and the pre-determined shop on-cost rate is 60% of direct labour. The actual indirect expenditure collected on the shop's On-Cost Work Order is Rs 7,80,000. The under-absorption of shop on-cost is:
e: Absorbed on-cost is Rs 7,20,000 against actuals of Rs 7,80,000, so Rs 60,000 of overhead was incurred but not recovered into job costs.

q: During a quarter, direct labour booked to a shop's jobs is Rs 8,00,000 and shop on-cost is absorbed at 60% of direct labour. The actual indirect expenditure of the shop is Rs 4,50,000. The position at the quarterly review is:
e: The rate recovered Rs 4,80,000 into jobs against actual overhead of Rs 4,50,000 — Rs 30,000 more than was incurred, i.e. over-absorption.

q: The works cost of a job executed for an outside body is Rs 3,20,000. Pro-forma on-cost is levied at 15%. The amount recoverable from the outsider on account of works cost and pro-forma on-cost is:
e: Pro-forma on-cost at 15% of Rs 3,20,000 is Rs 48,000, which is added to the works cost to ensure full cost recovery from the outsider.

q: The works cost of a deposit work for an outside body is Rs 1,60,000. Pro-forma on-cost is added at 15%, and thereafter a pre-determined profit of 10% is charged on the amount so arrived at (the profit percentage being fixed with Associate Finance concurrence). The total amount recoverable is:
e: Following the costing note's three-way pricing: works cost plus pro-forma on-cost gives Rs 1,84,000, and profit at 10% of that amount is Rs 18,400.

q: The works cost of a job done for an outsider is Rs 2,00,000. Pro-forma on-cost is levied at 15% of works cost and supervision charges at 12.5% of works cost. The amount recoverable before adding any profit element is:
e: Pro-forma on-cost (Rs 30,000) and supervision charges (Rs 25,000) are both added to the works cost in pricing outsiders' work.

q: A shop's actual indirect expenditure for a quarter is Rs 6,55,000, while the direct labour booked to its jobs in the quarter is Rs 10,00,000. The shop on-cost rate that would exactly recover the actual overhead is:
e: The required rate is actual overhead divided by direct labour; at the old 60% rate only Rs 6,00,000 would be absorbed, leaving under-absorption of Rs 55,000 — which is why the quarterly review raises the rate.

q: A wagon shop POHs 25 wagons in a quarter. Direct labour on the POH work orders is Rs 15,00,000 and direct material fitted is Rs 22,50,000. Shop on-cost is 60% and general on-cost is 15%, both on direct labour. The unit repair cost per wagon is:
e: Total POH cost is Rs 48,75,000; spread over 25 wagons, the unit repair cost is Rs 1,95,000 per wagon.

q: Which one of the following statements about pro-forma on-cost is NOT correct?

options.A: Pro-forma on-cost includes notional elements such as depreciation of workshop plant and buildings
options.B: Pro-forma on-cost charges can be waived by the WAO where the outsider is a deserving case
options.C: Pro-forma on-cost is levied on work done for other Government departments and outside parties
options.D: Pro-forma on-cost charges collected on deposit works are credited to Earnings (Abstract Z)

e: No lower authority can give away the Railway's overhead recovery: pro-forma on-cost can be waived only by the GM, with the concurrence of Associate Finance.
